QF.id: I Codes of Conduct and Investor Protection_21

question.text: The Investor Protection Fund (IPF) at a stock exchange is established for:

answer.text: Meeting legitimate non-speculative claims of clients of defaulting trading members

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 231-233 of the NISM Series I Currency Derivatives workbook (December 2025) describe the Investor Protection Fund (IPF) maintained at the stock exchange. The IPF is used to meet legitimate non-speculative claims of clients of defaulting trading members. The Trap: The IPF does not provide loans, pay dividends, or manage investor portfolios. It is also distinct from the company-law Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), which is not the subject of these workbook pages. Note: Page 233 separately permits up to 25% of the IPF's interest/income to be used for investor education and awareness, so investor education is a permitted use of IPF income but is not the fund's primary purpose.
